method: blind: P = the previous prompt ('a neon-lit bathhouse with terraced turquoise pools, ... arches, vaporwave'), Q = prompt naming the barrel-vaulted hall, terraced pool and round-arched arcades of mosaic tile (adopted); settled, walk1-3, rest and an 8-frame walking strip each, current build, headless WebKit

worst_flaw.old: almost nothing structural is painted: flat grey walls with magenta neon bands, a shapeless pink glow where the far wall should be, arches left as see-through outlines
worst_flaw.new: part of the painted stone arcade sticks to the screen and flickers (a pier narrows, the arch count changes between frames) while the see-through geometry arches slide past in front

ghosts: the same see-through arch outlines, white lines across the piers and seams across the pool in both (from the scene, not the painting); more visible in the old because its walls are blank. New: small dark human-like silhouettes inside the far doorway in walk1-2
notes: the old prompt is steadier from strip frame to strip frame, 'mostly because it has little to hold' (reviewer's rough raw luma change on the strips: 2.95 old vs 4.10 new; not motion-compensated)
over the longer walk the new keeps its identity (arcade and lit doorway in every frame); the old goes from tiled piers to a neon tunnel to stone arches to inflatable-looking tubes
summary: Q reads as one believable vaulted stone bathhouse whose arcades and lit doorway last from settled to rest; P mostly paints a flat foggy neon tube and keeps changing identity. P holds steadier frame to frame only because there is little to hold. Clear preference for Q.
